title: Factorial spikes separate componentwise Noetherianity from FI-Noetherianity
oneLine: A characteristic-free sub-FI-algebra has affine Noetherian components at every finite width but a strict infinite chain of FI-ideals across widths.
abstract: Let V(S)=k[x_s | s in S] be the standard width-one polynomial FI-algebra over an arbitrary field. This anonymous, unrefereed theorem candidate defines a sub-FI-algebra A generated by every FI-translate of g_r=x_1...x_(r-1)x_r^(r!) for r>=2. For each finite S, only widths r<=|S| occur, so A(S) is an affine, finitely presented Noetherian k-algebra. Globally, however, the FI-ideals J_R generated through width R form a strict infinite ascending chain. The exact obstruction is elementary: a native width-R spike could factor through lower widths only if the light-variable counts and peak exponents satisfied two simultaneous partition equations, while R!>(R-1)(R-1)! rules this out. The proof is characteristic-free. The regular A-module is finite free of rank one and contains a non-finitely-generated FI-submodule, which is a formal consequence over A rather than a non-free example or a module over V. The construction is not finitely generated as an FI-algebra; stronger finite-generation variants remain open. Producer-side exact replay, four hostile controls, a supplied release review and a five-role internal editorial gate support the candidate without establishing independent reconstruction, authenticated specialist review, formal verification, peer review, novelty or priority.
narration: Noetherianity usually means that ascending chains of ideals eventually stop. For an FI-algebra there are two scales to keep apart. At any one finite set, we see an ordinary commutative algebra. Across all finite sets and injections, we see an entire compatible system. This anonymous candidate separates those scales. In width r it introduces a monomial with r minus one light variables and one peak variable whose exponent is r factorial. At every fixed width n there are only finitely many such translated generators, so the component is an affine, finitely presented Noetherian algebra. But a genuinely new generator orbit appears at every larger width. The proof shows that the width-R spike cannot be assembled from smaller spikes: matching its light variables would use at most R minus one factors, while their total peak exponent is at most R minus one times R minus one factorial, strictly less than R factorial. The FI-ideals generated through successive widths therefore form a strict infinite ascending chain. The argument uses only monomials and integer exponents, so it works over every field. The regular module over the constructed algebra gives one carefully limited finitely presented-module consequence, but the construction is not finitely generated as an FI-algebra and it does not give a non-free module or a module counterexample over the original polynomial FI-algebra. This is release 0.1.0-candidate, dated 31 August 2026. It is anonymous and unrefereed. This AI-generated voice is a communication aid, not additional mathematical evidence.

problem.name: AIM representation stability problem list, section 1, item 1.2

keyResults: The displayed generators define a sub-FI-algebra A of V(S)=k[x_s | s in S] over every field.
Every component A(S) is finitely generated, finitely presented and Noetherian; for |S|=n there are n(2^(n-1)-1) distinct displayed generator monomials.
The FI-ideals generated by widths at most R form a strict chain J_2 strictly contained in J_3 strictly contained in J_4 and so on, so A is not FI-Noetherian.
The exact lower-width factorisation criterion separates light-variable accounting from peak-exponent accounting, and the factorial inequality rules out every lower-width factorisation.
The regular A-module is finite free of rank one and contains a non-finitely-generated FI-submodule; this does not give a non-free example or a module over the ambient polynomial FI-algebra V.
evidence: An eight-page DOI-bearing manuscript and aligned Markdown; a universal monomial proof; an exact native-width factorisation lemma and monomial-ideal membership lemma; dependency-free Python replay in normal and optimized modes; a structurally distinct ambient exponent-vector search through width seven; four hostile controls; an exact replay receipt; semantic metadata and raw-TeX checks; all-page visual inspection; source, citation and bounded novelty audits; the supplied release review; five differentiated internal editorial reports; one exact frozen-target confirmation; a 41-member ZIP containing 40 manifested payloads plus its root manifest; two successful public GitHub Actions runs; and exact unauthenticated GitHub and Zenodo asset readback. These establish availability, integrity, producer replay and the stated unrefereed candidate. They do not establish the universal theorem independently, authenticated specialist review, formal verification, editorial peer review, novelty, priority or impact.
statusDetail: Anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed FI-algebra theorem candidate after actioning a supplied full review, completing a five-role producer-coordinated editorial gate and passing one bounded confirmation on an exact frozen archive. Reviewer identity, specialist credentials and unaffiliated status were not authenticated. The literal unrestricted subalgebra and characteristic clauses receive a complete candidate proof; the regular-module corollary is deliberately scoped over A. The construction is not FI-finitely generated, and stronger finite-generation variants remain open.

humanJudgmentGates: Keep componentwise Noetherianity separate from Noetherianity of the FI-system.
State prominently that A is not finitely generated as an FI-algebra.
Scope the finitely presented module consequence over A and do not call it non-free or a module over V.
Treat finite replay and hostile controls as regression evidence for the encoding, not as proof of the universal theorem.
Keep the supplied review, internal editorial confirmation, authenticated specialist review, formal verification and peer review distinct.
Make no first-discovery or historical-priority claim from a bounded search.
